resource.name: Building Permits-Chicago
resource.description:
Update (October 15, 2025): A new field, PERMIT_CONDITION, is now part of this release.

The records span Chicago building permits from 2006 onward. Rows cover permits that remained valid after issue; those later voided or revoked are omitted. Permit categories generally require payment of the fee before construction may start—no work should proceed until fees are satisfied.
columns_description: Current status of permit (not available for all permit types).
Amount of building permit fees received
Amount of building permit fees due
The date when the permit was issued, which can help determine the likelihood of a permit being active or completed based on its age.
The category or type of the permit, such as residential, commercial, or industrial, which directly influences the permit status.
Type of applicant such as individual, company, or government entity, which might influence the processing and status of the permit.
The neighborhood or district where the building is located, which might have specific zoning laws affecting permit status.
The historical status of similar permits in the same area, which can indicate trends or common outcomes for permits.
The season during which the permit was issued, as construction activity can be seasonal and affect permit status.
The average time taken to process similar permits, which can indicate the expected status based on elapsed time since issue.
Economic conditions at the time of permit issue, such as recession or boom, which can affect construction activity and permit status.
The zoning code applicable to the permit, which can affect the complexity and status of the permit process.
A score representing the reputation or reliability of the contractor, which might influence the likelihood of permit completion.
